claim: Prospective hindsight (imagine the event has happened) is credited with about 30 percent more reasons in Mitchell 1989, but the figure is secondhand; the abstract points to certainty, not time frame, as the active ingredient.
agent_test: Same plan-failure prompt with 'has failed' vs 'may fail' wording at equal tokens; count distinct valid failure causes graded against known bugs.

claim: The only controlled human test of premortem against rival critique methods on plan confidence is Veinott 2010 (N=178 students, 5 conditions): premortem lowered confidence more. Exact means were not seen by any agent; a confidence drop is not an accuracy gain.
agent_test: Measure calibration (Brier) of agent self-confidence before and after a premortem step, not only confidence level.

claim: Premortem effects on counts of reasons depend on plan complexity: null vs Worst-Case Scenario on a simple plan (N=72), more reasons on a complex unfamiliar plan (N=82); categories of reasons differ by framing.
agent_test: Trigger premortem only on complex or unfamiliar tasks; compare against always-on at equal tokens.

claim: Behavioural evidence for premortem is one thesis experiment: 52 Army cadet teams, fewer fouls and less fixation, no test statistics seen.
agent_test: Replicate on a timed multi-step agent task with a behavioural outcome (errors committed).

claim: No preregistered replication, meta-analysis, or field trial with real plan outcomes of the human premortem was found; total controlled studies are about five and mostly student or small samples.
agent_test: Treat premortem as unproven; any adoption must be gated by our own equal-token ablation.

claim: Listing reasons against one's own answer reduces overconfidence (Koriat 1980), so listing reasons may be the mechanism, not the failure frame. No study crosses certain-failure framing with a reasons-against prompt.
agent_test: 2x2 on the agent: 'it failed' vs 'it may fail' framing x reasons-against vs neutral list.

claim: Devil's-advocate role-play can bolster the original view rather than diversify it (Nemeth 2001), and the failure frame is argued to beat it, but no direct comparison with numbers exists.
agent_test: Compare premortem prompt vs devil's-advocate prompt on same tasks.

claim: Debiasing by unpacking can backfire: in Hill 2012 (N=32) 78 percent showed subadditivity, and unpacking a residual shifted estimates, so listing failure causes can inflate probability of failure.
agent_test: Check that failure-cause listing does not push the agent's stated failure probability above observed error rate (overcorrection).

claim: Intrinsic self-critique without external feedback lowers accuracy: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 after 3 calls; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 to 89.0; debate does not beat majority vote. A bare premortem on the model's own answer carries this risk.
agent_test: Premortem must be signal-triggered and tied to an external check or tool; test ungated vs gated at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: LLM safety: failure-first prompting (InvThink) cut TRIDENT harmfulness from 3.22 to 2.19 (32 percent) vs SafetyPrompt 2.62, but a forward-direction control (PROTHINK, same 23,063 targets) gave equal safety, so the failure direction itself was not shown to matter.
agent_test: Run failure-first vs forward-first prompts matched in length on our reasoning tasks.

claim: InvThink gains are task-dependent: large on consequence reasoning (Illegal Activities +15.8), small on pattern matching; the trained version over-refuses (FRR 0.361 to 0.320 with tuned reward).
agent_test: Gate the check on task type; track false-alarm cost on benign items.

claim: Anticipatory 'what could go wrong with this action' reflection in an agent (Wang 2024) reached 23.5 percent success vs LATS 22.7 and post-failure reflection 19.8 after 7 episodes, with 45 percent fewer plan revisions; the gain over LATS is small and on WebArena-like tasks only.
agent_test: Pre-action failure query vs post-failure reflection at equal tokens on our tool tasks.

claim: Pre-action plan critique grounded in distilled past errors (PreFlect) improved GAIA total from about 46-50 to 58.18 (GPT-4.1); removing the error prior cost 7.9 points. Single run, small benchmark, and backbone assignment in the table layout is ambiguous.
agent_test: Re-run with and without a stored error-pattern memory at equal tokens, 3 seeds.

claim: The best forecasting agent wrote Pre/Post-mortem content in 37.8 percent of rationales vs about 12 percent for Opus 4.6; this is correlational, bundled with other dimensions, and expert review found only 24 of 130 worst questions had strategic errors.
agent_test: Ablate the pre/post-mortem dimension in the forecaster prompt and compare Brier.

claim: A post-mortem memory (Reflexion) improves later trials (HumanEval 91 vs 80 pass@1; reflection +8 over episodic memory), supporting stored failure lessons rather than in-the-moment imagination.
agent_test: Compare stored post-mortem lessons against premortem-only at equal tokens.

claim: Named 'prospective hindsight' and 'pre-mortem' in recent LLM work (AUGUR, Zhang 2026) are training methods with different mechanisms; they do not test the human premortem and should not count as evidence for a prompt step.
agent_test: none

claim: Close cousin debiasing (consider-the-opposite, Matern 2025) showed no compelling effect on self-assessment accuracy (+1.00 percent, CI -7.46 to 10.0), consistent with weak debiasing evidence in general.
agent_test: Low prior for any ungated debiasing step.

claim: PreFlect (GAIA, GPT-4.1) is resolved: 46.06 to 58.18 (+12.12). Removing the distilled planning-error prior leaves 50.30 and removing re-planning leaves 51.52, so stored error knowledge supplies most of the gain; 74% of plans were flagged risky, so the check nearly always fires.
agent_test: Ablate error prior vs imagined-failure prompt alone at equal tokens; log how often the check changes the plan.

claim: A failure check backed by an external tool beats a purely internal one. CRITIC: ChatGPT HotpotQA F1 42.8 to 52.9 with tools, 46.1 without; AmbigNQ 64.3 to 74.9 vs 67.3. Intrinsic self-correction without labels lowers accuracy (Huang: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1). A critical survey finds no general-task success from prompted-LLM feedback alone.
agent_test: Run the premortem step only when a test, tool or retrieval can check a named failure; compare against an internal-only step.

claim: Cheap triggers exist for gating a check: agreement among a few samples (Adaptive-Consistency: 3.3x fewer samples, under 0.1% accuracy loss on average) and P(True) calibration (Kadavath). No study has fired a premortem on these signals; the Peabody complexity effect is the only human gate evidence.
agent_test: Fire premortem when 3 quick samples disagree or when P(True) is below a threshold; compare with always-on and never-on at equal tokens.

claim: Stored failure lessons stack with retries and a prospective check: ExpeL matches Reflexion on HotpotQA (40% vs 39%) and gains from Reflexion on ALFWorld (59.0 to 64.2%); CoMem failure hypotheses grounded in retrieved cases beat Reflexion, DoT-Bank, ParamMem (HumanEval+ 95.09 vs 93.66, Qwen3-8B). No head-to-head with an imagined-failure prompt at equal tokens.
agent_test: Arms: premortem only, lessons only, both; equal tokens.

claim: No LLM study was found (arXiv, Crossref, Europe PMC, to Nov 2026) that prompts a literal premortem on a planning or coding task and measures accuracy against a no-premortem control; nearest work is bundled (Devil's Advocate, +3.5 over zero-shot, +0.8 over LATS) or trained (CoMem, InvThink).
agent_test: Our own ablation would be the first direct test.

claim: InvThink's matched forward-vs-failure SFT comparison showed no safety difference (both TRIDENT safety 1.000, ASR 0.000), and the SFT+RL model over-refuses (FRR 0.361; 0.320 with a calibration term). No LLM study measures stated failure probability inflation after listing failure causes (Hill's subadditivity is human-only).
agent_test: Measure over-refusal/hedging rate and Brier of the failure probability with and without the list.

claim: Pooling independent samples beats one pass for answers (self-consistency: GSM8K 56.5 to 74.4 with 40 samples) but costs the same multiple in tokens; pooling several independent failure lists has not been tested, and the group-vs-individual question for human premortem was not supported in the one poster found.
agent_test: Sample 3 failure lists, keep causes that recur, compare with one list at equal tokens.
